# Ignore the eval harness validation output dir (experience-out/) in .gitignore

## Problem statement

`npm run validate-experience` writes `experience-out/experience-validation.json` and `experience-out/experience-validation.md` into the working tree, but `experience-out/` is not in `.gitignore`. As a result, validation artefacts can be swept into `git add -A` and committed — this already happened once in commit `8d948f7b` (branch `dev`).

## Users

- Agent developers running baseline captures and experience validation locally.
- The `implement.py finish` pipeline which runs `git add -A` and must not commit generated artefacts.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `.gitignore` lists `experience-out/` beside the existing `eval-output/` entry, with an explanatory comment referencing this work item.
2. `experience-out/experience-validation.json` and `experience-validation.md` are removed from tracking via `git rm --cached` (files remain on disk locally).
3. A fresh run of `npm run validate-experience -- eval-output/balance-report.json` produces output in `experience-out/` and leaves `git status --porcelain` clean.
4. `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md` (or `docs/BALANCING.md`) states that the `experience-out/` output directory is git-ignored.
5. Full project test suite passes.

## Impact

Operators running experience validation will no longer have local artefacts accidentally committed to the repository.

## Constraints

- Files must remain on disk after `git rm --cached` (local availability preserved).
- Entry must be placed in `.gitignore` alongside the existing `eval-output/` rule for consistency.
- Documentation update should be a single sentence — no deep spec change.

## Existing state

- `.gitignore` contains `eval-output/`, `recordings/`, `capture-output/`, `perf-output/` — all local-only artefact trees.
- `experience-out/` is missing from this list.
- Two files (`experience-validation.json`, `experience-validation.md`) are currently tracked in the repo.

## Desired change

1. Add `experience-out/` to `.gitignore` with a comment referencing this work item.
2. Untrack the two committed files: `git rm --cached experience-out/experience-validation.json experience-out/experience-validation.md`.
3. Add a one-line note in `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md` that the output directory is git-ignored (or in `docs/BALANCING.md` if that is the more natural home).

## Key Files

- `.gitignore` — add the new entry
- `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md` — add git-ignore note
- `scripts/validate-experience.mjs` — reference only (to confirm output path)

## Related work

- **AH-0MVWAVJJG003S0XF** — Capture pre-change weapon balance baseline (parent/discovered-from; this item was found during that work).
- **AH-0MVSE1A7O002PXAO** — Journal the tune CSV edit (similar .gitignore + untrack pattern).
- **AH-0MU480XW8009160C** — Ignore the generated standups/ directory (precedent for .gitignore chore).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Removing tracked files may affect reviewers who rely on the committed validation files. *Mitigation:* files remain on disk locally; the commit message documents the change.
- **Assumption:** `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md` is the correct location for the git-ignore note; if `docs/BALANCING.md` is preferred, that is a minor adjustment.
- **Scope creep:** Do not modify `validate-experience.mjs` or the validation pipeline — only the gitignore and documentation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No questions raised — the work item is sufficiently defined.

# Capture/scripted setup grants loadout to the player only, so HUD upgrade rows omit it

> **Discovered while addressing AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9** (discovered-from:AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9) — the capture/scripted-setup counterpart of the hangar-war deployment fix.

## Problem statement

`applySceneSetup` (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`) grants capture/scripted setup
weapons only through `Player.equipWeapon(id, true)`, bypassing the
`EffectsRegistry`. Gyms that render the shared HUD build their upgrade rows from
`EffectsRegistry.activeWeapons()`, so a capture's permanent weapon has no row in
the upgrade list. The slot budget (`Loadout n/6`) counts it, but the visible list
does not — the same mismatch that AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9 fixed on the hangar-war
deployment path.

## Users

**Player running a gym with a capture setup that grants permanent weapons.**

> As a player running a gym whose capture setup grants permanent weapons, when I
> see the HUD upgrade list I expect it to show every permanent weapon I start
> with, so the list matches the `Loadout n/6` count and I can see what I have.

**Maintainer / future agent.**

> As a maintainer, I want capture/scripted setup permanent grants to run through
> the same grant seam as every other permanent grant, so the HUD, the player
> levels and the effect state can never drift apart again.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A gym (or scene) that applies a capture setup containing permanent weapons via
  `applySceneSetup` reports one slot-counted HUD upgrade row per granted weapon,
  matching a live-play run granted the same weapons through
  `grantPermanentWeapon`.
- The setup applier's documented ability to pre-grant more than
  `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` kinds is preserved (the capture divergence is unchanged).
- A regression test covers a setup-granted permanent weapon reaching both the
  `Player` and the `EffectsRegistry`.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Gyms that apply a capture setup with permanent weapons show those weapons in the
HUD upgrade list, so the list and the `Loadout n/6` count agree at a glance —
the same parity the hangar-war fix achieved for deployed loadouts.

## Constraints

- **The fix belongs in the shared applier `applySceneSetup`.** Gyms are the
  consumers; the applier lives in `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`. No gym is
  changed directly — only the applier's seam interface.
- **One permanent-grant seam.** Grants go through `grantPermanentWeapon`
  (`src/powerups/choiceReward.ts`) — the shared seam already used by hold-full
  rewards and checkpoint-resume replay.
- **The six-slot cap divergence stays.** A setup may pre-grant more than
  `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` kinds; the applier never consults the slot pool (AH-0MVVJS34M00551ES).
- **No second HUD data path.** The fix must not make the HUD derive weapon rows
  from the slot model; the HUD keeps rendering registry state.
- **Gyms with no player remain unchanged.** `applySceneSetup` already returns
  early for `getPlayer() === null`; no additional guard needed.
- **`hangarDeployment.ts` stays Phaser-free.** The registry reaches the applier
  through a structural seam, matching the pattern established by that module.

## Existing state

- `applySceneSetup` (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`) loops
  `setup.player.weapons` calling `player.equipWeapon(id, true)` — no registry
  grant. Same pattern for `weaponLevels`.
- Gyms call it via `{ getPlayer: () => this.player }` or `{ getPlayer: () => null }`;
  no registry seam is passed today.
- `CombatCoreScene._adoptCaptureSetup` (:336) is the central gym caller — it
  passes `this.player` from a `CombatCoreScene` subclass.
- `PlayScene` (:1419) also calls `applySceneSetup` with `this.player`.
- `grantPermanentWeapon` (`src/powerups/choiceReward.ts:80`) has the signature
  `(weaponId, effectsRegistry, player)` — exactly the two-surface grant needed.
- `PermanentWeaponRegistry` (`src/powerups/choiceReward.ts:60`) exposes
  `applyWeapon(id, permanent?): boolean` — a minimal structural interface that
  `EffectsRegistry` satisfies.
- **Precedent fix for the identical class of bug on the hangar-war path:**
  AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9 extended `HangarWarDeploymentSeams` with an optional
  registry seam and routed through `grantPermanentWeapon`.
- The hangar-war fix (`applyHangarWarDeployment`) still only grants through the
  registry seam it now exposes — it does **not** call `player.equipWeapon` itself,
  delegating entirely to `grantPermanentWeapon`. The scripted setup currently
  grants **only** through `player.equipWeapon`, so both surfaces (registry +
  player) must be touched.

## Desired change

1. Extend `SceneSetupSeams` with an optional effects registry seam
   (e.g. `getEffectsRegistry(): PermanentWeaponRegistry | null`).
2. In `applySceneSetup`, replace each
   `player.equipWeapon(id as WeaponId, true)` call for `setup.player.weapons`
   with `grantPermanentWeapon(id, registry, player)` — same for `weaponLevels`
   (one call per level).
3. Gyms and `PlayScene` that call `applySceneSetup` pass the registry through the
   new seam; callers without a player (or without a registry) keep today's
   behaviour.
4. Update the module doc-comment to state that setup grants are permanent grants
   through the shared seam.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts` — add the registry seam to `SceneSetupSeams`;
  route `applySceneSetup` through `grantPermanentWeapon`; update the module
  comment.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — pass `this.effectsRegistry` (or the
  structural equivalent) into the updated `applySceneSetup` call in
  `_adoptCaptureSetup`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — pass `this.effectsRegistry` into the updated call.
- `src/powerups/choiceReward.ts` — the seam consumed (`grantPermanentWeapon`);
  expect no change beyond a possible doc cross-reference.
- `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.test.ts` — extend to assert both the player grant
  and the registry grant for a setup-applied weapon.
- `src/scenes/gym/gymSceneSetupAdoption.test.ts` — extend existing gym tests to
  assert the registry grant.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — setup / capture section: grants are permanent
  grants through the shared seam and render as HUD rows.

## Risks & assumptions

- **A1 — the registry is the right store, not the HUD.** Same assumption as
  AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9: registering the grant (not a HUD-side fallback) is
  correct, per the documented single-seam precedent.
- **A2 — no double counting.** `grantPermanentWeapon` calls both
  `registry.applyWeapon(id, true)` and `player.equipWeapon(id, true)` — exactly
  the two surfaces the current code touches individually. No extra state is
  created.
- **Risk — callers without a registry.** Gyms like `GymHangar`,
  `GymCurveSequencer`, and `GymHexWar` pass `getPlayer: () => null` (no player).
  The new seam is optional; when absent the applier keeps today's behaviour
  (a no-op for these callers, which is correct since they have no HUD).
- **Risk — callers with a player but no registry seam.** Any gym that creates a
  player but does not supply a registry will lose the HUD row again. All combat
  gyms that have players should supply the registry; non-combat gyms (no player)
  are unaffected.
- **Risk — `weaponLevels` grant count.** A weapon with `weaponLevels[id] = n`
  currently calls `equipWeapon` n times; `grantPermanentWeapon` must also be
  called n times to match. The level increment (run-scoped) must remain correct.
- **Scope-creep risk.** The hangar-war deployment (`applyHangarWarDeployment`)
  was fixed in AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9; no change to that module. Timed weapons
  (`timedWeapons`) are intentionally left as non-permanent (`equipWeapon(id,
  false)`) — they are not permanent grants and should not be routed through
  `grantPermanentWeapon`.

## Related work

- AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9 — "Hex War doesn't add initial loadout to slots" (the
  hangar-war deployment fix — same pattern, different surface; committed as
  part of v0.1.21).
- AH-0MVSHI07B003BZIP — "When continuing HUD upgrades list is empty" (the
  checkpoint-resume precedent — permanent grants must touch registry + player;
  commit `4d9daf0b`).
- AH-0MVVJS34M00551ES — "Six-slot cap and the setup applier divergence"
  (documents why the applier is allowed to exceed the cap).
- AH-0MVVJSE9800339S6 — "Document six-slot HUD presentation and setup
  divergence".
- AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX — "Loadout can exceed the six-slot cap" (the slot cap
  guard).

## Duplicate-work check

Searched `setup HUD weapon row`, `applySceneSetup permanent weapon`, `capture loadout HUD`,
`scripted setup HUD row`, `sceneSetup effects registry`. The closest completed items
are AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9 (hangar-war deployment — same class of bug, different surface)
and AH-0MVSHI07B003BZIP (checkpoint resume — same class of bug, same class of fix).
None satisfies this item's acceptance criteria: the `applySceneSetup` → registry →
HUD path is unfixed. This is **not** a duplicate.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Should `timedWeapons` also be routed through `grantPermanentWeapon`?**
  — Answer: no. Timed weapons are `equipWeapon(id, false)` (non-permanent,
  countdown-based). `grantPermanentWeapon` is specifically for permanent grants.
  Timed weapons should not appear in the permanent HUD upgrade list. Source:
  `sceneSetup.ts` line `equipWeapon(id as WeaponId, false)`; the distinction is
  intentional.
- **Q: Does `CombatCoreScene` already hold a reference to the effects registry?**
  — Answer: yes — `CombatCoreScene` extends `Phaser.Scene` and has
  `this.effectsRegistry` (an `EffectsRegistry` instance) as a member, inherited
  from the scene composition. The seam can pass it structurally. Source:
  `CombatCoreScene.ts` member declarations.
- **Q: Are there any callers that pass a player but intentionally omit the registry?**
  — Answer: all combat gyms that create a player also compose an effects registry
  (they extend `CombatCoreScene` or implement the same seam). Non-combat gyms
  (`GymHangar`, `GymCurveSequencer`, `GymHexWar`) pass `getPlayer: () => null`.
  No known caller creates a player without a registry. Source: gym source files.
- **Q (open): None blocking.** No producer decision required. The fix approach
  follows the documented shared-seam precedent exactly.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVNW8UCZ004CY0R** – Director and registry: pass setup through start(key, setup) (completed)
- **AH-0MUX9T7C7003CBQP** – F3: Weapon temporary/permanent split (completed)
- **AH-0MUX9T7QA008CW73** – F4: Choice and HUD consume permanent/effective levels (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mvshi07b003bzip, 0mvvf0pov001jnkx, 0mvvjs34m00551es, 0mwcfkhwd002rkx9, ability (+316 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mvshi07b003bzip, 0mvvf0pov001jnkx, ability, absent, acceptance (+298 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: ability, absent, acceptance, add, additional (+269 more)

# Win path: suppress the mini-boss wheel and bank a fixed post-win bonus on hex wins (AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2)

Discovered-from: AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA (Re-baseline salvage, cores and the mini-boss reward value per hex deployment).

## Problem statement

With a hex deployment ending on its level's wave-10 mini-boss (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2), a winning deployment presents the mini-boss wheel reward **after** the run has finished (Q2 = b ordering: defeat → defence report → reward → map). The wheel's run-scoped permanent upgrades are applied to a completed run and have no further effect, so the post-win reveal reads as a broken reward. The producer's ruling on the OPEN QUESTION (recorded on AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA, 2026-11-13) is **Q1 = (c)**: suppress the wheel on the win path and bank a **fixed post-win bonus** into the hangar war instead.

## Users

- **As a Hangar War player**, after I win a hex deployment I want the post-win moment to pay into my persistent war (a banked bonus), not a wheel whose upgrades vanish into the finished run, so the reward reads as real progress.
- **As a producer**, I want the decision implemented exactly: arcade and loss paths keep the wheel as shipped; only the winning hangar deployment path changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Whole win-path reward surface suppressed on the winning hangar deployment path.** A winning hex deployment presents **no reward overlay** on the win path — neither `MiniBossWheelScene` nor the empty-owned three-option choice fallback (`pendingWinReward` is not carried); the player still sees the mini-boss defeat, then `DefenceReportScene` (which now announces the banked win bonus, Q3 = b), then the map. The bonus is banked as part of the win resolution. Pinned by a scene test through the shipped win-path wiring.
2. **Fixed post-win bonus banked — minerals, baselined from measurement.** The win resolution banks the fixed bonus as **minerals only** (Q2 = a) through the pure hangarWar banking/economy seams (`salvageBanking.ts` / `hangarEconomy.ts`), not a forked write. The amount is **baselined from AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA's measured per-deployment income** (Q1 = b; `wl dep` dependency on that item) and is stated as a named constant when set; this item does not invent the number. The banked balance is persisted through the one `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload write.
3. **Other paths unchanged.** The arcade campaign still shows the wheel on every mini-boss defeat, and a lost hangar deployment still shows no wheel and no bonus (report → map). Existing campaign/mini-boss suites pass without behavioural edits.
4. **Docs.** The GDD §8.2 win-path sentence (the "mini-boss **reward** overlay" / win-path reward line) and any affected code comments state the suppression + fixed mineral bonus on the winning hangar deployment path, the report announcement (Q3 = b), and the recorded decisions (Q1 = c, Q2 = a, Q3 = b; AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA), including any relevant wiki/docs-site entries.
5. **Full project test suite** passes with the new changes.

## Impact

A player who wins a hex deployment now sees their win bank real, persistent minerals into the hangar war — announced on the defence report instead of a wheel that spent its upgrades on an already-finished run.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — the hangar-deployment win-path transition (`_finaliseHangarWarMiniBossVictory` / `_resolveHangarWarWinReward` / `_resolveHangarWarCapture`); suppress the wheel and bank the bonus.
- `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.ts` — the win-path reward presentation seam; replace the wheel reveal with the banked-bonus announcement (Q3 = b).
- `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts` / `MineralChoiceScene` — unchanged surfaces (still the arcade/gym rewards); the win path simply no longer launches them.
- `src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — the pure banking/economy seams the bonus writes through.
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — the payload fields (`bankedMinerals` / `bankedCores`) the bonus lands in.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.captureCycle.test.ts`, `src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.hexMiniBossVictory.test.ts` — the seams to pin.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 — the win-path economy notes to update.

## Constraints and assumptions

- **Bonus amount baselined from measurement (Q1 = b).** The amount is derived from AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA's measured per-deployment income once that lands; this item has a `wl dep` dependency on it for the number, and the number is recorded on the item (as a named constant) when set. No invented number here.
- **Minerals only (Q2 = a).** The bonus banks minerals; cores are not granted by the win-path bonus (a captured deployment already banks its one core via the capture cycle — adding bonus cores would double-count).
- **Win path only.** Suppression is scoped to winning hangar deployments; nothing else moves (gym↔game parity for the shared wheel surface stays intact — the wheel remains the arcade/gym reward).
- **Pure seams.** All bonus banking resolves in `src/core/hangarWar/`; scenes only wire it.
- **Announced, not silently banked (Q3 = b).** `DefenceReportScene` announces the banked bonus before the map so the win "reads as real progress".
- **"The wheel" = the whole win-path reward surface.** The recorded decision suppresses the win-path *reward overlay* — the wheel and the empty-owned fallback choice alike, since both grant run-scoped value to a finished run (recorded interpretation of Q1 = c, 2026-11-13).
- **Scope-creep guard.** A change to banking rules, prices, the bonus amount's balance, unlock pacing, or the measured income itself is a further linked item, not folded in here.

## Existing state (researched, with evidence)

- **Win path wiring exists.** `PlayScene._finaliseHangarWarMiniBossVictory` resolves capture, resolves the win reward (`_resolveHangarWarWinReward` → `drawWheelOutcome`/`buildWheelWedges`/`applyWheelOutcome`, or the empty-owned three-option choice), stores `pendingWinReward`, then transitions via `DefenceReportScene`, which launches the wheel overlay (`_presentReward`), then the map. The wheel's `applyWheelOutcome` grants run-scoped permanent levels to the finished run (`src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts:348`).
- **Pure banking seams.** `bankSalvage` (salvageBanking.ts) copies cumulative minerals + cores with a per-run watermark; `resolveHexCapture` (captureCycle.ts) banks the run's salvage and marks the hex; `hangarEconomy.ts` holds `CORE_MINERAL_EQUIVALENT = 100` and the pricing/purchase rules; the balance persists via `hangarWarStore` in the `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload.
- **The GDD §8.2 win-path sentence** currently reads "…the mini-boss **reward** overlay (the same shared `MiniBossWheelScene` the arcade uses) …" — this is the sentence AC4 updates.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: the measurement dependency is still open.** The bonus amount waits on AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA's measured per-deployment income (Q1 = b); until it lands, the named constant is provisional and AC2's amount assertion is pinned once set. The banking/wiring change does not depend on the number (only the value does).
- **Assumption: suppression covers the empty-owned fallback too.** The recorded decision (Q1 = c) is read as removing the *whole* win-path reward overlay, not just `MiniBossWheelScene`; an empty-owned win must not present the three-option choice either (it also grants run-scoped value). If the producer intended the fallback to survive, AC1 narrows accordingly.
- **Scope-creep risk:** re-tuning the bonus amount, banking rules, prices or unlock pacing is a further linked item, never folded in here.

## Related work

- **Re-baseline salvage, cores and the mini-boss reward value per hex deployment (AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA)** — records the producer decision this implements (Q1 = c) and is the source of the measured per-deployment income the bonus amount is baselined from (blocking `wl dep` dependency).
- **In HexMap killing the mini-boss wins the hex (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2)** — the parent change that introduced the post-win reward positioning.
- **Win-path reward after the defence report (AH-0MWCOW6KA008OJOL)** — the change that introduced the win-path reward ordering this item suppresses/replaces (completed).
- Repository references: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 / §4.4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md`, `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/{salvageBanking,hangarEconomy,captureCycle}.ts`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MWCOW6KA008OJOL** – Win-path reward after the defence report (completed)
- **AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA** – Re-baseline salvage, cores and the mini-boss reward value per hex deployment (open)
- **AH-0MWCOW4IQ003XST5** – Mini-boss victory captures the hex and ends the run (completed)

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — What is the fixed post-win bonus amount, and what rules the knob?**
  - Asked: 2026-11-13 (intake, producer-review round 1). Answered 2026-11-13 (producer, interactive reply).
  - Question: The recorded decision (Q1 = c on AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA) suppresses the wheel on the win path and banks a fixed post-win bonus, with the amount a balance knob either producer-specified or baselined from that item's measured per-deployment income.
  - Options: (a) producer-specified now; (b) baselined from AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA's measured income once it lands (blocks this item on the dependency); (c) freeform.
  - **Recommended: (a).** — a concrete number now makes AC2 fully testable immediately without waiting on the open measurement item.
  - **Answer (producer): (b)** — the amount is baselined from AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA's measured per-deployment income once it lands; recorded as a named constant, `wl dep` dependency on that item.
  - Status: **ANSWERED** (recorded in AC2 / Constraints).
- **Q2 — What does the fixed bonus pay out in?**
  - Asked: 2026-11-13 (intake, producer-review round 1). Answered 2026-11-13 (producer, interactive reply).
  - Options: (a) minerals only; (b) cores only; (c) fixed package.
  - **Recommended: (a)** — cores are the scarcer currency and already bank one per capture; a mineral grant reads naturally.
  - **Answer (producer): (a) minerals only.**
  - Status: **ANSWERED** (recorded in AC2 / Constraints).
- **Q3 — Does the player see the banked bonus on the win path?**
  - Asked: 2026-11-13 (intake, producer-review round 1). Answered 2026-11-13 (producer, interactive reply).
  - Options: (a) silently banked; (b) announced in `DefenceReportScene` ('win bonus banked: +N' before the map); (c) freeform.

# Hangar War: leave the defending bot with the run's permanent upgrades

## Problem statement

When a hex deployment is won, the bot left behind carries only the **catalogue** hull rating (`baseDefence + 3 × armour + 2 × firepower + 2 × systems` of the hull as authored in the hangar catalogue), so everything the ship actually earned during that sortie — permanent weapon levels, permanent power-up levels and owned consumable charges — is discarded at the moment of victory. A player who clears a hex with a heavily upgraded ship leaves a bot no stronger than a bare hull, which makes the capture's "leave a bot" step feel disconnected from the run that earned it.

## Users and user stories

- **Player (primary).** "When I beat a hex's mini-boss, I want the bot I leave behind to keep the permanent upgrades my ship had at that moment, so the run I just flew is what defends the hex."
- **Player, reading the map.** "When I look at a held hex, I want to see what the defending bot is made of — its upgrade contribution and total rating — so I can judge whether the next frontier attack will hold."
- **Designer/tuner (secondary).** "I want the upgrade → rating conversion in one documented table, so retuning defence strength never needs a code change or a save migration."

## Existing state

- `leaveDefender` (`src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts`) builds the `HexDefender` with `defenceRating = deriveDefenderRating(hullId)`, plus optional boss-typed `skills` from the hull and equipped modifiers.
- `deriveDefenderRating` / `defenderRatingFromUpgrades` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) are the single rating formula, fed only from the hangar catalogue.
- `HexCaptureInput` carries `hexId`, `defenderHullId`, `salvage`, `definitions`, `banked`, `tuning` — **no run-upgrade snapshot**.
- At the mini-boss victory the run does hold the data: `Player.getWeaponLevels()`, `Player.getPowerUpLevels()`, and `PowerUpLevelStore.snapshotConsumablePools()` (read by `_saveCheckpoint` for the arcade path, `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`).
- The defender is never flown; every defence is arithmetic over stored numbers (`resolveDefence`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`).
- Design of record explicitly says the rating comes from the hull's hangar upgrades only: GDD *capture cycle* step 3 and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D (intake assumption A4). This item changes that rule.
- The frontier aggression budget is sized from `resolvePlayerStrength(hangar)` — hangar progression only — and the *between-sortie tick* compares each held hex's stored rating against `baseAttackingForce (2) + origin aggression × 1`, scaled by `100 + 15 × aggression` % ± 10 %.

## Desired change

1. **Snapshot the run at victory.** `resolveHexCapture` accepts the run's permanent-upgrade snapshot and `leaveDefender` persists it on the `HexDefender` as an **additive optional field** (same back-compat pattern as `skills`): permanent weapon levels, permanent power-up levels, and the owned consumable charge state.
2. **Convert it with the hull's own vocabulary.** The snapshot contributes to the rating through one documented mapping table, so the rating stays a single number the resolver compares:

   | Source | Stat bucket | Weight |
   |---|---|---|
   | every permanent weapon level (any weapon) | firepower | 1 point per level |
   | permanent level of a **defensive** power-up kind (Shield, Force Field, Thorn Field, Bomb, Smart Bomb, Phase Shift) | armour | 1 point per level |
   | permanent level of every other power-up kind (Teleport, Speed Boost, Frenzy, Chrono, Magnet, Mineral Scoop, Mystery UFO, Salvage, Strike, Mining Laser) | systems | 1 point per level |
   | each held **defensive** consumable charge (Shield, Force Field, Thorn Field) | armour | 1 point per charge |
   | each held **other** consumable charge (Mystery UFO) | systems | 1 point per charge |

   Then `defenceRating = hullRating + 3 × armour + 2 × firepower + 2 × systems`, reusing the shipped `defenderRatingFromUpgrades` weights so there is still exactly one rating formula.
3. **Show the numbers.** The map's held-hex detail panel and the between-sortie defence report list the bot's stored upgrade breakdown next to the existing hull/skills lines, so a hold or fall that depended on upgrades is legible.
4. **One code path for the game and the gyms.** `GymHexWar`'s "leave bot" control surface takes the same snapshot and renders through the shared helpers (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity); no second derivation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `leaveDefender` / `resolveHexCapture` persist the run's permanent-upgrade snapshot on the `HexDefender` and derive `defenceRating = hullRating + 3 × armour + 2 × firepower + 2 × systems`, where the stat buckets come from one exported, documented mapping table that classifies **every** `WeaponId` and `PowerUpId` (a test fails if a catalogue id is unclassified).
- A defender captured with no permanent upgrades produces exactly today's payload and today's `defenceRating` (the new field is omitted when empty), so existing saves, fixtures and replays are unchanged; a save written before this change still loads and resolves as before.
- The `HexMapScene` held-hex detail panel and the between-sortie defence report show the left bot's stored armour/firepower/systems, the upgrade rating contribution and the total rating, alongside the existing hull and skill lines; `GymHexWar` leaves an upgraded bot through the same shared leave/derive/render code and displays the same numbers, with no divergent copy of the conversion (parity asserted by test).
- Tests cover: the mapping table (every id classified, unknown ids ignored), derivation totals, corrupt input (negative / fractional / non-finite snapshot collapses without throwing), the no-upgrades equality case, capture-cycle persistence and omission, `HexDefender` store round-trip/migration, and a `PlayScene`/`HexMapScene` assertion that a mini-boss victory persists the flown run's upgrades on the defender.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically GDD *capture cycle* step 3, the GDD defender-rating formula section, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D (assumption A4) and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` for the gym control surface.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player who wins a hex can now leave behind a bot that keeps the permanent upgrades the ship had when the mini-boss fell, and can read on the map exactly what that bot is worth.

## Out of scope

- Changing `resolvePlayerStrength` or the `DEFAULT_FRONTIER_TUNING` constants (producer decision Q3 = A).
- Carrying the run's **temporary** (timed) weapons or field-pickup state into the defender.
- Carrying held minerals, score or remaining lives onto the defender (not upgrades — see Assumptions).
- Any new defender behaviour in combat: the bot is still never flown; the defence stays arithmetic over stored numbers.

## Verification (manual)

1. Deploy at an unheld hex from the map, deliberately collect several permanent upgrades during the sortie, then beat the wave-5 mini-boss.
2. Re-open the map, focus the newly held hex and confirm the detail panel lists the upgrade breakdown and a total rating greater than the bare-hull rating.
3. Run one between-sortie tick and confirm the defence report shows the same stored rating on the attack row.
4. Repeat in `GymHexWar`'s leave-bot control surface and confirm identical numbers.

## Constraints

- **Pure and injectable:** the conversion and the derivation stay in the pure core (`captureCycle` / `hangarEconomy`), no Phaser, no storage access; the scene only supplies the snapshot and persists the returned payload.
- **No schema version bump:** the new field is additive/optional and read by field presence, matching `skills`, `frontierTick` and the contract fields.
- **One rating formula:** the resolver keeps comparing one stored `defenceRating`; nothing new enters `resolveDefence`.
- **Producer decisions recorded in this intake:** Q1 = B (weapon levels + power-up levels + owned consumable charges), Q2 = B (hull weights: armour 3 / firepower 2 / systems 2 via a per-kind mapping table), Q3 = A (the frontier aggression budget is **unchanged** — defence simply gets easier).
- **Balance consequence accepted (Q3 = A):** with shipped tuning the attack strength tops out near 26–28, so an upgrade contribution in the tens makes a held hex mathematically unretakeable, and the between-sortie tick's retake pressure effectively disappears for well-defended hexes.
- CHANGELOG.md is out of scope (managed by the release pipeline).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — new optional `HexDefender` upgrade-snapshot field (additive, omitted when empty).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — the mapping table, the snapshot → stat-bucket reducer and the extended rating derivation.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — `HexCaptureInput` gains the snapshot; `leaveDefender` / `resolveHexCapture` thread it through and record it on the defender.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — supplies `getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` / `snapshotConsumablePools()` at the mini-boss victory capture, in the same place the checkpoint snapshot is taken.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — defensive parsing of the new optional field (round-trip, migration by field presence).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` and `src/core/hangarWar/defenceReport.ts` — intel lines and report numbers for the stored breakdown.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — renders the new intel lines (shared with the gym).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — the "leave bot" control surface passes the snapshot and shows the same numbers.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — the rule change and its documented consequence.

## Related work

- Hangar War: capture cycle — hex deployment, boss-granted discovery and defending bot (AH-0MVUXCAW0001VUM6) — the module this changes.
- Pure defence resolver and frontier aggression clock (AH-0MVUXCA0J0011W88) — records the "rating from the hull's hangar upgrades, never a live battle" rule this item revises.
- Post-MVP Hangar War: upgraded defending bots with special skills (AH-0MVWZYJ740037EZ1) — the precedent for adding stored defender data additively.
- Versioned ai_hell_hangar_war store with migration (AH-0MVUXC0M5007LCGV) — the back-compat pattern the new optional field follows.
- Hangar economy and unlock tree (AH-0MVUXC1GQ00366Z6) — owns `deriveDefenderRating`, the weights and `resolvePlayerStrength`.
- Between-sortie defence report and attract-mode traversal (AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP) — the report surface that must show the new numbers.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Balance risk (highest):** with Q3 = A the frontier cannot outgrow upgraded defenders. A late run's upgrade contribution can exceed the maximum possible attack strength, so hexes become permanently safe and the war's retake tension goes quiet. *Mitigation:* the conversion lives in one exported table with one weight per bucket, so a follow-up tuning item can cap or rescale without touching saves; the risk should be measured from real runs before any such item is filed.
- **Save-compatibility risk:** an additive optional field on `HexDefender` must be omitted when empty and parsed defensively, or existing saves/fixtures drift. *Mitigation:* the `skills` pattern exactly; a store round-trip test and a "pre-change save loads unchanged" test.
- **Inflation risk:** consumable charge state changes between the mini-boss moment and the capture write if read at different points. *Mitigation:* read the whole snapshot once, in the same expression that feeds `resolveHexCapture`.
- **Design-document drift risk:** GDD step 3 and Candidate D A4 state the hangar-only rule; leaving them stale contradicts shipped behaviour. *Mitigation:* the docs AC names both files.
- **Scope-creep risk:** candidates deliberately excluded — changing `resolvePlayerStrength` (Q3 = A), retuning the frontier tuning constants, and carrying the run's *temporary* (timed) weapons into the defender. Each is a separate decision and must become its own work item rather than growing this one.
- **Assumption:** "permanent upgrades present at the end of the mini-boss battle" means the permanent levels and owned consumable charges the ship held at victory; held minerals, score and remaining lives are **not** upgrades and are not carried.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q3 — Should the frontier aggression budget grow to match upgraded defenders?** Options: (A) leave the budget alone (defence gets easier); (B) count held defenders into `resolvePlayerStrength`; (C) cap the per-bot upgrade contribution. — **Answer (operator):** **A** — the budget is unchanged; the easier defence is accepted. *Research:* `resolvePlayerStrength` is fed from the hangar only, and tick attack strength derives from `baseAttackingForce: 2`, `forcePerOriginAggression: 1`, `aggressionPercentPerPoint: 15`, `jitterPercent: 10` (`DEFAULT_FRONTIER_TUNING`), i.e. a maximum near 26–28.

# Strengthen a hexes defence

Problem statement: A player who owns a hex has no way to spend their banked salvage to make the bot defending it stronger. This item adds an "Upgrade Defences" flow: select a held hex on the map, open a hangar-style upgrade screen targeting that hex's bot, and spend minerals/cores on hangar-catalogue upgrades that fit the bot's ship.

## Users (with user stories)

- **Player (primary).** "When I select a hex I own, I want to send upgrades to the bot defending it, so the salvage I earned strengthens a hold I care about."
- **Player, making a purchase.** "I want to buy upgrades with minerals and/or cores from the Hangar, and only those that fit into the bot's existing ship — an upgrade to a weapon it already carries, or a new weapon in an empty slot."
- **Player, after a tick.** "I want the upgrades to stay on the bot between sorties, and to be gone for good if the hex loses its defence, so spending salvage is a real commitment."

## Acceptance Criteria

- Selecting a **held** hex on the hex map surfaces an `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action; activating it opens the bot-upgrade screen for that hex's defender. An unheld hex offers no such action, and the read-only `GymHexWar` map render never offers it either.
- The bot-upgrade screen reuses the shared hangar-screen model/renderer pattern (game and `GymHangar`/`GymHexWar` parity): it lists the hangar-catalogue entries (weapons, hulls and modifiers) and shows each one's fit verdict for the focused bot — **upgrade existing** (the bot already carries the weapon → raise its level), **add to empty slot** (a weapon kind the bot does not carry → offered **only** when the bot has a free permanent slot), **re-hull** (a hull entry), **train** (a modifier entry), or a disabled reason (slot pool full / unaffordable / ring-gated). No second, drifting copy of the fit rule exists.
- A purchase is paid for in minerals and/or cores from the fleet's banked salvage (the hangar wallet, `HangarState.bankedMinerals`/`bankedCores`), spends exactly the displayed price, and applies the upgrade to the bot's ship: a new weapon kind occupies one permanent slot at level 1, an already-carried weapon rises one level, a hull entry swaps the bot's `hullId` (keeping the existing carried loadout), and a modifier entry applies its effect to the bot. The fleet's owned sets, active hull/loadout and the player's deployed ship are untouched by a bot purchase.
- Weapon upgrades follow a **per-level upgrade price** (Q9 = B): a separate, authored upgrade-price rule for raising an already-carried weapon's level, distinct from the catalogue entry's purchase price for a new kind; both are documented in one pricing table.
- The bot's defence rating reflects the sent upgrades through the **one** existing rating formula (`defenderRatingFromSnapshot` / the `UPGRADE_STAT_BUCKETS` mapping); a purchase returns a fresh payload with the defender's stored `defenceRating` recomputed and re-persisted, never a second derivation.
- Upgrade state persists on the `HexDefender` across between-sortie ticks and save/load round-trips (additive optional fields, field-presence migration, same pattern as `skills`), and is destroyed with the bot when its hex falls in a defence tick (existing `applyDefence` path — a fallen hex loses its defender).
- Tests cover: the fit rule (upgrade-existing vs add-to-empty-slot vs re-hull vs train vs disabled states), purchase economics (price, per-level upgrade price, wallet deduction, refused purchases), snapshot update + rating recompute, persistence round-trip and fall-destruction, corruption tolerance of the stored upgrade state, the map action surface and the gym parity assertion.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` for the new bot-upgrade control surface.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player can now spend earned minerals and cores to send hangar upgrades — weapons, hulls and modifiers — to a bot defending a hex they own, and read the strengthened rating on the map; giving the hangar economy a second, defence-shaped sink.

## Constraints

- **Pure and injectable:** the fit rule, purchase application and rating recompute live in the pure core (hangar economy / a new `botUpgrade` module), no Phaser, no storage access; scenes only present and persist.
- **Same-data-model rule (producer Q2):** the bot uses the same ship data model as a player-controlled ship — the permanent slot model (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` = 6 shared weapon/power-up slots) and the victory-snapshot vocabulary from `AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ` (`DefenderUpgradeSnapshot`: permanent weapon levels, power-up levels, consumable pools). The bot is never flown; its loadout is stored data that feeds the one rating formula.
- **Hangar catalogue entries (producer Q3):** the upgrade pool is the shipped `HANGAR_CATALOGUE` — **weapons, hulls and modifiers** (producer Q10 = "everything") — no new economy, no new currency; ring gating and prices reused as authored, plus the new per-level weapon-upgrade price (Q9 = B).
- **Slot-fit rule (producer Q8 = A):** a weapon the bot does **not** already own is offered **only** when the bot has an empty permanent slot; a weapon the bot already carries is always offered as a level-upgrade. Hulls and modifiers have no slot requirement (a hull swaps `hullId`, a modifier applies its effect).
- **One interaction (producer Q4):** an `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action in the hex summary section opens a version of the player-ship upgrade scene (the hangar screen) scoped to the bot — same screen pattern, different purchase target.
- **Destruction (producer Q5):** upgrades are persistent **unless** the hex loses a defence tick, which destroys the bot (today's `applyDefence` already unholds the hex and drops its defender; nothing new to build there).
- **Rating (producer Q6):** upgrades change the stored `defenceRating`, recomputed through the single shipped formula.
- **No player-ship effect (producer Q7):** a bot purchase never touches the player's deployed ship, active loadout or the fleet's owned sets.
- **No schema version bump:** new optional fields read by field presence, matching `skills` / `frontierTick`.
- CHANGELOG.md is out of scope (managed by the release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `HexDefender` (`src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`) is a derived-rating record — `hullId`, `defenceRating`, `bankedMinerals`, optional `skills` — with no weapon slots or upgrade levels. It is never flown; every defence is arithmetic over stored numbers.
- The sibling item (AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ) lands the bot ship-model vocabulary in the economy: `DefenderUpgradeSnapshot`, `UPGRADE_STAT_BUCKETS` (one frozen row per `WeaponId`/`PowerUpId`), `defenderStatBuckets`, `snapshotDefenderUpgrades`, and `defenderRatingFromSnapshot` — already merged (commits `46d217b5`, `58dc8edc`). Its capture-cycle threading is being delivered through its own child items (e.g. AH-0MWHF6ZHW0058SMX); **this item depends on that snapshot existing on `HexDefender`** (dependency edge recorded).
- The player-ship slot model is the permanent six-slot pool shared by weapons and power-ups (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` in `src/core/constants.ts`, `capDropIdsToSlotPool` in `src/powerups/slots.ts`).
- The hangar economy (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) owns prices, `canBuy`/`buy`, `purchaseWeight`, ring gating and `resolvePlayerStrength`; the catalogue (`src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`) holds hulls, starting weapons and modifiers with two-currency prices.
- The hangar screen (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) is the pure model + one renderer used by the shipped hangar scene **and** `GymHangar`; the hex map (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` + `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`) renders focused-hex intel in the right-hand detail panel, with held hexes selectable but not actionable.
- Defence ticks (`runFrontierTick` → `applyDefence`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`) already destroy a fallen hex's defender (`held=false`, `defender=null`).

## Desired change

1. **Bot ship model.** `HexDefender` carries the shipped upgrade-snapshot vocabulary (permanent weapon/power-up levels, consumable pools) as additive optional fields, alongside the existing hull/rating/skills — the same-data-model rule (Q2). The bot's slot occupancy derives from the stored levels against `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`.
2. **Fit rule (pure).** A new pure function answers, per catalogue entry and per defender: `upgrade-existing` (bot already carries the weapon → level +1), `add-to-empty-slot` (new weapon kind, **only when a free slot exists**), `re-hull` (hull entry, no slot requirement), `train` (modifier entry, no slot requirement), or a disabled reason (slot pool full, unaffordable in either currency, ring-gated). The fit rule and the hangar's `canBuy` combine into one verdict per row.
3. **Per-level weapon-upgrade price (Q9 = B).** One authored table defines the upgrade price for raising an already-carried weapon's level (distinct from the catalogue's new-kind purchase price). Both prices appear on the row and are paid from the hangar wallet.
4. **Purchase application (pure).** Spending the displayed price applies the upgrade to the defender's ship: a new weapon kind enters at level 1 in one permanent slot, an already-carried weapon rises one level, a hull entry swaps `hullId` keeping the carried loadout, a modifier entry applies its effect; `defenceRating` recomputes through `defenderRatingFromSnapshot` / the buckets mapping — one formula (Q6). A refused purchase returns the payload unchanged.
5. **Map action.** The held-hex detail panel (the "hex summary section") gains an `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action; `HexMapScene` wires it to open the bot-upgrade screen for the focused defender (Q4). Unheld hexes offer nothing; the gym's read-only render (no handlers) offers nothing — parity by construction.
6. **Bot-upgrade screen.** A hangar-screen-style scene scoped to one defender: same pure model + one renderer shape as `hangarScreen`, showing the fit verdicts, both price kinds and the bot's current loadout/rating; purchases return a fresh payload that the scene persists. Game and gym (if exercised) share the model/renderer so they cannot drift.
7. **Persistence and destruction.** Purchases persist via the versioned store (additive optional fields, field-presence parse). A defence-tick fall destroys the bot including its upgrades through the existing `applyDefence` path (Q5).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — `HexDefender` gains additive optional upgrade-snapshot fields (weapon/power-up levels, consumable pools) mirroring `DefenderUpgradeSnapshot`.
- `src/core/hangarWar/botUpgrade.ts` (new) — the pure fit rule, the per-level upgrade-price table (Q9 = B), purchase application and per-row verdict for a defender's upgrade options (own module so the scenes never derive a fit).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — any shared helper the purchase needs (wallet spend, snapshot → rating via existing `defenderRatingFromSnapshot`).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — defensive parse/round-trip of the new optional fields (field presence).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` and `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — the held-hex `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action row + activation wiring in the detail panel.
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — handler wiring (`onUpgradeDefences(hexId)` → open the bot-upgrade screen) and the route back after a purchase.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/botUpgradeScreen.ts` (new) + `src/scenes/hangarWar/botUpgradeScene.ts` (or a mode of the existing hangar screen) — the pure model + one renderer for the bot-upgrade screen.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` (and `GymHangar` if it renders the upgrade screen) — parity/no handlers for the new surface.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, README — the new control surface and its parity entry.

## Related work

- **Hangar War: leave the defending bot with the run's permanent upgrades (AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ)** — dependency: supplies the `DefenderUpgradeSnapshot` model, the stat-bucket mapping and the snapshot-aware rating this item's purchases consume; its capture-cycle threading first puts the snapshot on `HexDefender`.
- Hangar economy and unlock tree (AH-0MVUXC1GQ00366Z6) — owns `canBuy`/`buy`, prices and ring gating the purchase path reuses.
- Capture cycle — hex deployment, boss-granted discovery and defending bot (AH-0MVUXCAW0001VUM6) — the module that creates `HexDefender`s.
- Hex-map intel / map screen (AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2) — the detail panel that gains the `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action.
- Post-MVP Hangar War: upgraded defending bots with special skills (AH-0MVWZYJ740037EZ1) — precedent for additive optional defender fields and the skills pattern (modifier `train` applies here).
- Versioned `ai_hell_hangar_war` store with migration (AH-0MVUXC0M5007LCGV) — the back-compat pattern new optional fields follow.
- Between-sortie defence report and attract-mode traversal (AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP) — the tick path that destroys a fallen bot (Q5).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Balance risk (highest):** spendable upgrades let a player push a held hex's rating high, making well-defended hexes mathematically unretakeable — the same accepted consequence as the sibling item's Q3 = A. *Mitigation:* one rating formula and one mapping table, so a follow-up tuning item can cap or rescale prices without touching saves; measure from real runs before filing.
- **Pricing granularity risk (Q9 = B):** the per-level weapon-upgrade price is new authored data; its exact progression is a balance knob. *Mitigation:* one documented table in `botUpgrade.ts`, authorable without code changes; defaults chosen conservatively at implement time and reviewed in the effort/risk notes.
- **Dependency risk:** the brief assumes the sibling's snapshot-on-`HexDefender` threading lands first. If it slips, this item's data model cannot build. *Mitigation:* dependency edge recorded; implement after the sibling's capture threading.
- **Save-compatibility risk:** new optional fields must be omitted when empty and parsed defensively, or existing saves/fixtures drift. *Mitigation:* the `skills` pattern exactly; store round-trip + pre-change-save tests.
- **Wallet-conflict risk:** bot purchases spend the same banked minerals/cores the player uses for fleet unlocks — a bot spend can starve the hangar. *Deliberate per Q3/Q8 (A):* catalogue-priced, shared wallet; documented rather than gated in this item.
- **Modifier-fit risk (Q10 = everything):** a modifier whose effect targets run stats (e.g. `extra-lives`) has no bot meaning; only modifier effects with a stored-bot effect (e.g. `defence-skill`) can be sent. *Mitigation:* the fit rule classifies modifier effects by whether they change stored defender data; `extra-lives`-style effects are shown disabled with a reason rather than silently charged.
- **Scope-creep risk:** candidates deliberately excluded — a bot that is actually flown in combat, any new currency, new catalogue entries, and any change to player-ship progression or the frontier tuning constants. Each excluded candidate must become its own work item rather than growing this one.
- **Assumption (Q8, A):** the upgrade screen offers every catalogue entry the fleet can afford (ring + wallet gating), subject to the slot-fit rule for new weapons; a purchase spends banked salvage without granting the fleet an unlock — the bot gets the entry, the fleet does not.
- **Assumption (Q9, B):** a per-level upgrade-price table governs raising an already-carried weapon's level; a new weapon kind pays the catalogue purchase price and enters at level 1, occupying one permanent slot when one is free.
- **Assumption:** "permanent slots" for the bot mean the shared six-slot weapon/power-up pool (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`), counted by distinct permanently-carried kinds — the bot's stored data, never a live battle.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 — "What does 'send upgrades for the ship' mean?" — **Answer (operator):** upgrade the **defending bot** (the bot left in the hex). *Source:* interactive reply.
- Q2 — "Does the bot get its own slot system?" — **Answer (operator):** the bot should be the **same as a player-controlled ship**, using the same data model so it has **slots etc.** *Research:* `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` (six shared weapon/power-up slots) and the sibling item's `DefenderUpgradeSnapshot` are the vocabularies this maps onto.
- Q3 — "What counts as an upgrade the player can send?" — **Answer (operator):** **hangar catalogue entries**, purchased with minerals and/or cores from the Hangar. *Research:* `HANGAR_CATALOGUE` + `canBuy`/`buy` already implement two-currency, ring-gated purchases.
- Q4 — "What's the UI interaction?" — **Answer (operator):** add an **"upgrade defenses" button to the hex summary section**, which opens **a version of the player-ship upgrade scene (hangar)** but upgrades the bot instead of the player's ship.
- Q5 — "Persistence and limits?" — **Answer (operator):** **persistent unless it loses a defence tick, in which case it is destroyed** (matches today's `applyDefence`: a fallen hex unholds and drops its defender).
- Q6 — "How does the upgrade affect the bot's defence?" — **Answer (operator):** it **changes the defence rating** (recomputed through the one shipped formula).
- Q7 — "Does sending upgrades affect the player's ship?" — **Answer (operator):** **no**.
- Q8 — "Which catalogue entries can the player send?" — **Answer (operator):** **A** — every catalogue entry the fleet can afford, spending banked salvage without granting the fleet an unlock — **refined**: a weapon the bot does **not** already own is offered **only** when the bot has an **empty slot**. *Source:* interactive reply (round 2).
- Q9 — "How does 'upgrade to an existing weapon' price?" — **Answer (operator):** **B** — a **separate per-level upgrade price** (its own authored pricing table), distinct from the catalogue purchase price for a new kind. *Source:* interactive reply (round 2).
- Q10 — "Which catalogue kinds are in scope?" — **Answer (operator):** **everything** — weapons, hulls and modifiers are all sendable (each with its own fit rule; hulls re-hull, modifiers apply their stored effect). *Source:* interactive reply (round 2).

# Capture cycle threads the run snapshot

Child of AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ. `HexCaptureInput` accepts the victory-moment snapshot, `leaveDefender` records it on the defender, and the stored `defenceRating` becomes hull rating **plus** the snapshot's weighted contribution — still one number for the resolver.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, when I beat a hex's mini-boss, I want the bot I leave behind to keep the permanent upgrades my ship had at that moment, so the run I just flew is what defends the hex.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `HexCaptureInput` gains an optional permanent-upgrade snapshot; `leaveDefender` / `resolveHexCapture` persist it on the `HexDefender` and derive `defenceRating = hullRating + 3 × armour + 2 × firepower + 2 × systems` through the C2 helpers.
- A capture with **no** permanent upgrades produces exactly today's payload and today's `defenceRating` — asserted by deep-equality against the pre-change result — and omits the new field.
- An upgraded capture's stored rating is `bare hull rating + contribution`, proven for both a weapon-heavy and a defensive-power-up-heavy snapshot.
- The cycle stays pure and injectable (no Phaser, no storage); nothing new enters `resolveDefence` — the resolver still compares one stored `defenceRating`.
- Capture-cycle tests cover persistence, omission and the corrupt-snapshot case; the C1 capture specs go green.

- **Parent AC restated (AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ):** `leaveDefender` / `resolveHexCapture` persist the run's permanent-upgrade snapshot on the `HexDefender` and derive `defenceRating = hullRating + 3 × armour + 2 × firepower + 2 × systems`, where the stat buckets come from one exported, documented mapping table that classifies **every** `WeaponId` and `PowerUpId` (a test fails if a catalogue id is unclassified).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add the snapshot field to `HexCaptureInput` in `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` and pass it to `leaveDefender` in the same call that already threads the hull and banked minerals.
- In `leaveDefender`, derive the rating from the C2 snapshot-aware derivation, attach the normalised snapshot only when non-empty, and keep the skills block untouched.

- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.test.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`

## Dependencies

C3 (the persisted field must exist before the cycle can record it).

## Deliverables

- Threaded snapshot through the capture cycle with the extended rating derivation and tests.

# Update Hangar War time budget: 5–15 minutes per hex

## Problem statement

The Hangar War outer-loop budget is authored as per-ring windows (ring 1: 40–60 min,
ring 2: 90–120 min), but a player experiences pacing one deployment at a time — one
hex, one level. Both current windows are missed by the measured baseline
(ring 1 grind 16.4 min, ring 2 grind 48.1 min), so the authored budget should be
re-expressed at the unit the player actually experiences: **5–15 minutes per hex
deployment**, with per-ring totals derived from it (ring 1, 6 hexes → 30–90 min;
ring 2, 12 hexes → 60–180 min).

## Users

- **Producer** — authors the pacing target once, at the per-deployment unit, instead
  of maintaining per-ring windows; the derived ring totals follow automatically.
- **Developer** — implements and verifies the budget; needs a harness that gates on
  the new budget and a report that states both the per-hex window and the derived
  per-ring windows, with verdicts re-computed rather than re-worded.
- **Player** — a hex deployment (one level as the five-wave sortie) should feel like
  a 5–15 minute commitment; a whole ring stays an evening's play (30–90 / 60–180 min).

Example user stories:

- As a producer, I want the budget authored as 5–15 minutes per hex so that the
  pacing target is stated at the unit a player actually experiences.
- As a developer, I want `npm run ring-timing` to gate on the new budget and print
  the per-hex window plus derived per-ring windows so a regression is caught in CI.
- As a developer, I want the rebalancing items (ring 1: AH-0MWFDQ9EY004NO4X, ring 2:
  AH-0MWFDQCFV007BZE5) re-ruled against the new budget so the recorded evidence
  stays truthful.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `RING_TIMING_TARGETS` (or the equivalent authored budget in `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`) expresses the 5–15 min per-hex budget; per-ring totals derive from it (ring 1: 30–90 min, ring 2: 60–180 min for 6/12 hexes).
2. `npm run ring-timing` gates on the new budget: the text report prints the per-hex window and the derived per-ring windows, and the current measured baseline is re-rated against them.
3. `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` is regenerated on the new budget and the measured tables in `docs/EVALUATION.md` and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Session shape (and the GDD §8 and README mentions of the authored windows) are requoted to match; earlier measured figures are recorded, never re-worded.
4. Tests in `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` (and any docs-assertion tests, e.g. `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts`) are updated to the new budget and pass through the test skill; determinism and the real-arena evidence tests still hold.
5. The open rebalancing items AH-0MWFDQ9EY004NO4X (ring 1) and AH-0MWFDQCFV007BZE5 (ring 2) are re-ruled against the new budget via dependency edges and comments (recorded, not closed by this item).
6. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, GDD, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Impact

# Hangar UI: buy to upgrade owned weapons and power-ups

## Problem statement

The hangar economy today treats every catalogue entry as **binary ownership**: `canBuy`/`buy` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) spend minerals/cores to add an entry id to the owned sets (`unlockedHulls`, `unlockedWeapons`, `ownedModifiers`), and an entry the fleet already owns is refused with `owned`. There is **no path for the player to buy an upgrade** — i.e. spend hangar currency to raise the **permanent level** of an already-owned weapon or power-up — even though permanent levels are the run's own vocabulary (`Player.getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()`, and `PowerUpLevelStore.snapshotConsumablePools()`), and even though the capture cycle now carries exactly those permanent levels onto the defending bot (AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ). The existing Hangar screen (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`, `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts`) renders unlock rows whose `HangarUnlockState` ends at `owned` (`BUY` / `OWNED` / `RING 2` / `NEED N min`) with no upgrade action.

## Goal (user story)

As a player in the hangar, I want to spend my banked minerals/cores on upgrading weapons and power-ups I already own — raising their permanent level — so the hangar is a place to grow my fleet between sorties, and so the bot I leave behind in a hex (which keeps my permanent upgrades at capture time, AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ) can be strengthened from the hangar, not only by what I happen to collect in a run.

## Impact

Players can spend banked minerals/cores in the hangar to permanently upgrade the weapons and power-ups they already own, so the fleet grows between sorties and a captured defender inherits the upgraded permanent levels.

## Design constraints (bear in mind — do NOT implement here)

This item must NOT be implemented as part of AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ; that epic only ships the **capture-side** snapshot. This item is filed so the code and UI design of the upgrade path stays compatible with what that epic introduced:

- The upgrade path should feed the **same** permanent-level model the snapshot reads: `Player.getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` (permanent components only; temporary/timed stacks must never be purchasable) and the consumable pool state (`PowerUpLevelStore.snapshotConsumablePools()`).
- Upgrade **pricing/gating** should extend the existing economy's rule set (`canBuy` precedence `owned → gated → unaffordable`, ring gating via `minRing`, two-currency `HangarPrice`) rather than introduce a parallel purchase rule; a deliberately separate item because "buy another level" changes the `owned` refusal semantics into an upgrade-branch of the economy.
- The hangar screen's unlock rows should gain an upgrade affordance for owned rows without breaking the existing `BUY`/`OWNED`/`RING 2`/`NEED N min` rendering or the attract-mode booth (cheapest-useful-unlock) decision (`decideHangarAction`).
- Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md): the upgrade rule must live in the pure economy (no Phaser, no storage), consumed by `HangarScene` and `GymHangar`/`GymHexWar` alike; no divergent copy.
- A defender captured after an upgrade must persist the **already-upgraded** permanent levels (no extra storage change needed: the capture read happens at victory time; the upgrade just means the accessors return higher levels).

## Assumptions (to confirm during planning)

- The upgrade ceiling/cap (`max level` refusal) comes from the **existing** permanent-level ceiling used by the run upgrade path, not a new parallel number; the economy rule reads the same ceiling.
- The per-level price curve (e.g. a scaling multiplier per level) is left to implementation but must be deterministic and use the existing two-currency `HangarPrice` conventions.
- `costToUpgrade`/`buyUpgrade` are suggested names; the contract (pure, non-mutating, refusal on unknown/unowned/temporary/capped ids) is the requirement, not the names.
- Scope-creep guard: reward-axis purchases into a held hex (AH-0MWH48IEG00929GQ) and hull upgrade bays (AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY) are **out of scope** here — this item only converts an already-owned weapon/power-up into a higher permanent level.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Economy rule.** `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` gains a pure upgrade rule (e.g. `costToUpgrade` / `buyUpgrade` beside `canBuy`/`buy`): given an owned weapon/power-up id and current permanent levels, it returns a two-currency price (using the existing `HangarPrice`/ring-gating conventions, with an explicit cap/ceiling so an already-maxed kind is refused), never mutates its inputs, and refuses unknown/unowned/temporary ids.
2. **Persistence.** Buying an upgrade raises the **permanent** level (weapon level / power-up level) in the same persisted state `getWeaponLevels()`/`getPowerUpLevels()` read, survives a save/load round-trip and a replay, and never touches temporary/timed stacks (`getTempWeaponIds()`/`getTempPowerUpIds()` stay empty after a purchase).
3. **UI affordance.** The hangar screen's owned row for a weapon/power-up shows the current level and an upgrade action with its price (e.g. `UPGRADE · 25 min`), disabled visibly when the player cannot afford it or the kind is capped; the existing `BUY`/`OWNED`/`RING 2`/`NEED N min` rows for non-upgradeable kinds are byte-identical to today.
4. **Capture integration.** A capture resolves against the upgraded permanent levels: a hex captured after the player buys upgrades leaves a defender whose `upgradeSnapshot`/`defenceRating` reflect the higher levels (asserted through the shared capture path, AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ).
5. **Parity and tests.** The upgrade rule is exercised by both `HangarScene` and the gym harness through the one pure economy function (no second derivation; duplicate-body guard green), and unit tests cover: price, cap refusal at max, unaffordable, unknown/unowned/temporary refusal, save/load round-trip, and the capture integration assertion.
6. **Docs.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 / the hangar section and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D record the buy-to-upgrade path as the intended upgrade source (distinct from the run-economy pickup path), and any code comment that says upgrades come only from runs is corrected.
7. **Full suite green.** Full project test suite passes with the change (via the test skill; the dev-push gate enforces it).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — the pure upgrade rule + price/gating/cap (extending the existing economy conventions).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts` — economy tests.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — owned-row upgrade affordance + level display (shared renderer).
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — buy-to-upgrade handler persisting via the store.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts` (or the shared hangar harness) — gym parity.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` / the permanent weapon-level store — the permanent-level grant seam a purchase writes through.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — the upgrade-source rule.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ** (this item is discovered-from) — capture-side: the defending bot keeps the run's permanent upgrades; the upgrade-buy path must feed the same permanent-level model.
- **AH-0MVUXC1GQ00366Z6** — Hangar economy and unlock tree (completed; owns `canBuy`/`buy`, `resolvePlayerStrength`, the weights).
- **AH-0MWUXCAG90086LH2** — Hex map scene with known-ahead intel (completed; the hangar link A5).
- **AH-0MWH48IEG00929GQ** — Strengthen a hexes defence (open; map-purchase flow for *sending* upgrades into a held hex, related but separate purchase surface).
- **AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY** — Post-MVP hull upgrade bays as a reward axis (open; the hull-side upgrade concept — watch for overlap when hull upgrades become purchasable).

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D** – Hangar War deployments start with no extra weapons in the loadout (default weapon only) (completed)
- **AH-0MVUXC1X6007KAG1** – Hangar scene: unlock tree and deployment/loadout selector (completed)

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mweusvj1007exjy, acceptance, accessors, action, add (+294 more)
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, accessors, action, add, afford (+275 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: acceptance, accessors, action, add, agents (+240 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required — the seed context (discovered-from epic AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ, the existing economy/screen code, and completed precedent AH-0MVUXC1GQ00366Z6 / AH-0MVUXC1X6007KAG1) already specified the problem, constraints and measurable acceptance criteria. Answer (Map, intake agent): proceeded without interview. Research: inspected `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` (canBuy `owned → gated → unaffordable`, `HangarPrice`, `minRing`) and `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` (`HangarUnlockState`, `BUY`/`OWNED`/`RING 2`/`NEED N min` rendering); find-related report at `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MWHW4ALS0039JFU.md`.
- Q: "Upgrade ceiling/cap source: the item assumes the max-level refusal cap comes from an existing permanent-level ceiling in the run path. None exists (weapon levels unbounded per `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`; power-up levels unbounded above; `isPowerUpAtDiscreteCap` is a gym disable rule, false for continuous-only kinds). Where does the cap come from?" — Answer (producer, 2026-11-15): **option (a)** — introduce **one shared, documented max-permanent-level ceiling constant** (e.g. `MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL`) read by both the run-path level-up offer and the hangar economy; deterministic cap refusal in the pure economy; preserves the "no parallel number" intent by single-sourcing the number. Research: `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` ("levels are unbounded but the value never exceeds a finite cap"), `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` (`isPowerUpAtDiscreteCap`, unbounded levels). Final: (a).
- Q: "Which owned kinds are upgradeable? Consumables (shield, phase_shift, teleport, force_field, mystery_ufo, thorns) never level up in the run path (charges, not levels); extra_life is field-pickup-only." — Answer (producer, 2026-11-15): **option (a)** — the upgrade rule applies to **level-bearing permanent kinds only** (weapons + non-consumable power-ups: bomb, speed_boost, magnet, mineral_scoop, smart_bomb, frenzy, chrono, salvage, strike, mining_laser); consumables/field-pickup-only kinds are refused as non-upgradeable (no permanent level to raise) and their rows stay byte-identical; charge purchases stay out of scope. Research: `src/powerups/types.ts` `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` consumable/fieldPickupOnly flags; `src/powerups/choice.ts` charge-vs-level offer dispatch. Final: (a).

question: Planning needs two producer decisions before the feature plan can be decomposed (the economy-rule contract and the UI upgrade-affordance scope both depend on them). Code research is complete; neither answer exists in the repo or worklog.

Q1 — Upgrade ceiling/cap source. The item's assumption states the max-level refusal cap 'comes from the existing permanent-level ceiling used by the run upgrade path, not a new parallel number; the economy rule reads the same ceiling'. Verification shows no such existing ceiling: weapon levels are unbounded (src/utils/weaponLevels.ts: 'levels are unbounded but the value never exceeds a finite cap'), power-up levels are unbounded above, and isPowerUpAtDiscreteCap is a gym manual-assign disable rule that returns false for continuous-only kinds. Options: (a) introduce one shared, documented max-permanent-level ceiling (a constant both the run-path level-up offer and the hangar economy read — single source of truth, deterministic cap refusal); (b) author per-kind max levels in hangar catalogue data as the one ceiling both read; (c) derive the cap from full curve saturation, which is technically unusable for continuous-only kinds. Recommended: (a) — one shared ceiling constant consumed by both run path and hangar economy, preserving the 'no parallel number' intent by making it a single authored number.

Q2 — Which owned kinds are upgradeable. Consumable power-ups (shield, phase_shift, teleport, force_field, mystery_ufo, thorns) never level up in the run path — permanent grants add charges, never levels; extra_life is field-pickup-only. 'Buy to upgrade' per the item raises a permanent level. Options: (a) the upgrade rule applies to level-bearing permanent kinds only (weapons + non-consumable power-ups: bomb, speed_boost, magnet, mineral_scoop, smart_bomb, frenzy, chrono, salvage, strike, mining_laser); consumables/field-pickup-only kinds are refused as non-upgradeable (no permanent level to raise) and keep today's rows byte-identical. Recommended: (a) — matches 'raises the permanent level' and 'never touches temporary/timed stacks', and keeps charge purchases out of scope (per the scope-creep guard). (b) would additionally allow buying consumable charges from the hangar — an expansion beyond this item.

Proposed feature-plan shape once answered (approx 6 features, test-first): (1) economy-rule contract tests (red-first), (2) pure costToUpgrade/buyUpgrade in hangarEconomy.ts, (3) persist permanent levels through the hangar payload + grant seam, (4) hangar owned-row upgrade affordance + level display, (5) GymHangar/GymHexWar parity + capture-integration assertion (AC4, needs capture epic on dev), (6) docs (GDD 8.2 / Candidate D) + full-suite verification.
